name: 901 Navajo Street (Cranes Landing)
award: 2023 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Mercy Housing Mountain Plains is building 901 Navajo Street, renamed Cranes Landing: 190 income-restricted homes (94 permanent supportive, 96 family units at 30% to 60% AMI) with an American Indian/Alaska Native focus and an on-site clinic run by Denver Indian Health and Family Services, on Denver Housing Authority land by the 10th & Osage light rail station; it won 2023 Round Two federal 4% and state credits with $46.4M of CHFA bonds, broke ground in March 2025 and was pre-leasing in August 2026.
why_it_matters: It shows how a D3 housing authority ground lease, 94 city-funded project-based vouchers, a 99-year city covenant and a separately financed New Markets clinic condominium can be stacked under one 4% bond deal to serve a specific underserved population within fair housing rules.

status.label: Under construction (groundbreaking 2025-03-20); pre-leasing since 2026-08-24, opening expected December 2026
status.detail: The contractor's construction start was reported on 2025-01-13 and the ground blessing and groundbreaking took place on 2025-03-20. The building topped out in November 2025; Mercy began pre-leasing on 2026-08-24 and its leasing page says it opens in December 2026, while a February 2026 article put first residents in January 2027. No financing closing date was published; closing is inferred from the start of construction.

next_step: Watch for the certificate of occupancy, which starts the 20-year city rental subsidy term, and for the opening of the clinic in early 2027.

background.text: The site was bought in 2020 for about $4 million through a City of Denver and Denver Housing Authority partnership for supportive housing, funded by bonds backed by the Affordable Housing Fund mill levy; DHA chose Mercy through a competitive process and it is DHA's sixth site under that program.
The 94 supportive units are reserved for people experiencing homelessness with a disabling condition: 81 one-bedroom, 5 two-bedroom, 6 three-bedroom and 2 four-bedroom units, per the application.

Mercy designed the building with the Native American Housing Circle, holding focus groups with American Indian and Alaska Native community members; the plan includes a round traditional gathering space, and fair housing rules mean the property cannot exclude other qualifying applicants.

The project had to build two new street segments (extending 9th Avenue and Osage Street as shared streets); the city vacated a strip of right-of-way at 901 Navajo (ordinance 24-1207, passed 2024-10-09) and accepted dedications of North Osage Street and West 9th Avenue deeded by DHA in November 2024 (resolution 24-1792, adopted 2025-01-06).

A July 2023 Phase II study found low-level tetrachloroethylene below groundwater standards on a former coal and petroleum storage site; the budget covers removal of contaminated soil under a materials management plan.
The market study put the family-unit capture rate at 51.5% and the supportive-unit capture rate at 15.5%, with 3.3% vacancy at area tax credit properties.
The application targeted a September 2024 closing; construction started in early 2025, and Mercy reported topping out in November 2025.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award description gives 112 one-bedroom, 41 two-bedroom, 31 three-bedroom and 6 four-bedroom units, while the Denver loan agreement designates 109 one-bedroom, 49 two-bedroom, 26 three-bedroom and 6 four-bedroom units.
The 2023 announcement described 187 units, while CHFA, the city and later reports give 190.
The clinic is described as 16,000 square feet by the contractor announcement and as 18,000 square feet by Mercy and the Colorado Trust.
Mercy's leasing page says the property opens in December 2026, while the Colorado Trust reported residents would not move in until January 2027.
The total cost including the clinic was estimated at $85 million in 2023 and reported as $111 million in 2026.
